video_title: Matt Hougan: The 4 Crypto Assets Winning This Bull Market
gist: Bitwise's Matt Hougan argues the new crypto bull market is driven by two ten-year trends, Bitcoin as a debasement hedge and tokenization/stablecoins, with DeFi tokens (Uniswap, Chainlink) improving economics via buybacks while fundamentals still lead price.

insights.claim: Matt Hougan (Bitwise) argues tokenized stocks win first at the edges of the traditional market (after hours, weekends, holidays, and when leverage is wanted) rather than competing with brokerages at 11:00 New York time, following the usual pattern of technological disruption.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Look for tokenized-equity volume to grow in off-hours niches before it threatens mainstream venues.
insights.quote: It never goes after the mainstream application. It works on the edges.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid provided oil-market liquidity during the early stage of the Iran war while the rest of finance was closed, which Hougan calls an important moment because it pushes users outside their comfort zone and they then tend not to leave.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Crisis-hour liquidity is a customer-acquisition channel for on-chain venues.

insights.claim: The interviewer watched the Nvidia earnings call and could trade Nvidia on Hyperliquid immediately afterward, seeing a 10% down, 20% up price move; Hougan says every hedge fund and macro trader wants to trade earnings in real time, and today only tokenized venues allow it.
insights.speaker: Host
insights.so_what: Earnings-window trading is a concrete wedge for tokenized equities.

insights.claim: Hougan says the market is over-focused on perfecting the tokenized instrument's structure (SPV versus native tokenization); users just want the most liquid, accessible version, and over time it will move to natively tokenized assets or collateralized debt vehicles like European ETPs.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Counterparty risk on tokenized stocks is real but secondary in this early phase; pick large branded issuers with much at stake.
insights.quote: you want to align with big brands that have a lot at stake

insights.claim: On-chain settlement happens in about a second, versus a day in the US and two to four days in some markets, so Hougan expects 'DeFi' to become just 'finance' and crypto to be 'on-chain finance'.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Settlement speed is the structural argument for the migration of asset trading on chain.
insights.quote: I think DeFi will just be finance

insights.claim: Hougan lists four requirements for traditional finance to move on chain: working tech, ease of use, assets with real fundamental value, and peer examples plus regulatory comfort; the last is just coming into focus as BlackRock, Apollo and Harvard's endowment act as pioneers.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Fast followers will enter after pioneer moves; the Clarity Act is helpful but not the binding constraint.

insights.claim: Hougan says blockchain technology is now fit for purpose (high throughput, reliably low cost, account abstraction), unlike 2017 and DeFi summer when fees hit $20-50 and Solana went down, which is why he expects this bull market to be more robust than prior ones.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Infrastructure bottlenecks that capped previous cycles have largely been removed.

themes.theme: DeFi revival and fundamentals ahead of price

insights.claim: Hougan cites three DeFi catalysts: protocols turning on fee switches (Uniswap running roughly $100-150 million of annual token buybacks), expansion into real-world assets, and Robinhood Chain integrating Uniswap and Morpho from day one on an Arbitrum chain.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Buyback-backed DeFi tokens now have investable cash-flow mechanics that governance-only tokens lacked.
insights.quote: a hundred to a hundred and fifty million dollars in annual buybacks

insights.claim: Hougan argues DeFi protocols' addressable market grew roughly 100x when moving from a roughly $2 trillion crypto market to $100-150 trillion of stocks and $300 trillion of bonds, and that the market has not yet recognized how big this change is even after Uniswap's token roughly doubled.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Blue-chip DeFi tokens may still be early in repricing for tokenized RWA TAM.

insights.claim: Uniswap's token was only a governance token with no value-capture mechanism because the SEC under Gary Gensler would have deemed value capture an illegal securities offering; that regulatory pressure has lifted.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Regulatory change is the root cause of improving token economics across DeFi.

insights.claim: Hougan says narrative and data are currently moving before price in crypto, citing Robinhood Chain discussed on Crypto Twitter in July while Wall Street upgraded Robinhood stock only at the end of August, a roughly two-month window; he expects this to fade as sentiment turns more bullish.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Alpha comes from tracking on-chain usage and partnerships early, but the window narrows as the bull matures.

insights.claim: Hougan expects the more bullish stance on Uniswap and Morpho because early integrations create winners: Robinhood's integration should help them win more such TradFi deals, though he stresses diversification.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Back DeFi protocols that TradFi entrants integrate first.

themes.theme: Exchange competition, Hyperliquid and capital formation

insights.claim: Hougan notes derivatives leadership in crypto has rotated from BitMEX to Binance to now possibly Hyperliquid, so the category has not been sticky; he says Coinbase and Binance have escape velocity while smaller centralized exchanges will see a dispersion of winners and losers.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Expect market share churn in derivative venues and pressure on sub-scale centralized exchanges.

insights.claim: Hougan says Hyperliquid's success came from combining six or seven existing advances (perps, order books) with good UX at the right moment, and expects repeats of this 'rhyming' pattern, including an ICO 2.0 now that the SEC has greenlit capital raising.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Revived ideas from past cycles with better projects can produce a new wave of token capital formation this cycle.

insights.claim: Hougan expects social trading apps like FOMO to become 10x-20x bigger than today and says he is bullish on the theme but bearish on the returns of participants; he notes 78% of large-cap professional funds underperformed the S&P 500 this year.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Own the platform theme rather than expecting users' returns; governments may restrict portfolio talk.
insights.quote: I'm not actually bullish on the returns of people who are engaged in FOMO investing

insights.claim: Hougan sees paired stock-meme coin products as likely ephemeral in their current economics but thinks the primitive of attaching a token to a real asset on a bonded liquidity curve will have a second and third life.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Watch for token-to-asset pairing primitives rather than the current memecoin versions.

themes.theme: Institutional demand, stablecoins and Bitwise strategy

insights.claim: Hougan says institutional interest in stablecoins and tokenization is vastly greater than six months ago, with flows into Bitwise funds capturing the theme since the market stabilized in July and a multi-billion-dollar advisor inbound nearly every day, whereas earlier price weakness (falling 20% a month) blocked buying.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Price stabilization converted a year of institutional education into flows.

insights.claim: Hougan attributes a wave of bank consortia and multi-billion-dollar acquisitions by Stripe and MasterCard to the GENIUS Act, and expects similar entry points and institutional investment in tokenization six to twelve months after regulatory progress.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Stablecoin M&A is a template for a tokenization M&A wave in 2027.

insights.claim: Hougan says Bitwise is strategically shifting toward on-chain products (vaults, staking after acquiring two staking firms including Core One, and automated token portfolios of tokenized stocks) and agrees that in ten years tokenized versions would outweigh ETFs.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Asset managers are positioning for ETF disintermediation by on-chain wrappers.
insights.quote: we're fully confident that the future of finance is on chain

insights.claim: Hougan has no strong view on whether new TradFi layer ones such as Robinhood Chain and ARC will compete with existing chains, expecting them mostly to broaden the market with winners and losers, citing PayPal USD as a failure alongside successes like Circle.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Treat TradFi chain launches as market expanders and avoid assuming success.

insights.claim: Hougan says his Mount Rushmore basket remains Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and Chainlink, with Hyperliquid, Zcash (privacy) and Venice (AI) as challengers; Bitcoin is the debasement play and the other three are tokenization exposure.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: A simple core allocation framework: Bitcoin for debasement, the rest for tokenization.

insights.claim: Hougan argues current tokenomics are the worst they will ever be for almost every crypto asset, that regulatory relief creates a one-way improvement toward buybacks, and that this underpins his bullishness on Chainlink, Uniswap and Aave.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Improving token economics is a multi-year tailwind across blue-chip tokens.
insights.quote: the current tokenomics are the worst that they will ever be

insights.claim: Hougan's token economics checklist is revenue capture with buybacks, clarity on unlocks (he says unlocks have killed more projects than they helped), reduced inflation, avoiding value split between token and equity holders, and ownership transparency.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Use this checklist to screen tokens; avoid low-FDV launches with perpetual unlock cliffs.
insights.quote: unlocks have killed more projects than they've helped

insights.claim: Hougan frames Hyperliquid and similar deflationary-supply tokens as 'exhaustible commodities' that can be valued with methods dating to the 1930s, arguing this is arguably as good as equity for value capture.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Commodity-style valuation models may fit buyback-heavy tokens better than equity analogies.

insights.claim: Hougan calls Bitcoin the best risk-adjusted bet in crypto and 'digital gold', arguing it will perform differently from the rest of the ecosystem, driven by US debasement such as proposed trillion-dollar checks and $2.5 trillion deficits during robust growth.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Fiscal expansion is the core Bitcoin driver, independent of altcoin cycles.

insights.claim: After eight years of being ignored, Hougan says traditional investors in the last six months have started considering moving a 60/40 portfolio to 90/10 fiat versus hard assets (Bitcoin and gold), which could drive Bitcoin to multiple hundreds of thousands of dollars.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: A small portfolio-weight shift by mainstream allocators is the upside mechanism for Bitcoin.
insights.quote: you could see a price measured in multiple hundreds of thousands of dollars

insights.claim: Hougan argues the debt cannot be grown away because governments spend extra revenue from growth, so even AI-accelerated growth would be matched by spending, worsening the debt problem; higher rates create a wealth effect concentrated in bondholders who can buy hard assets.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Higher rates and deficits can be Bitcoin-positive through bondholder income redirected to hard assets.

insights.claim: Hougan says Bitcoin rallied from 60 to 80 (thousand) and stuck the landing since July, and identifies debasement and the rise of stablecoins and tokenization as the two ten-year mega trends, advising long-term holding since mega trends pay out unevenly over years.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Position for ten-year trends and expect drawdowns along the way.

insights.claim: Hougan says some smart people argue AI agents will use stablecoins and DeFi protocols rather than dollars and centralized protocols, which he finds very true though with uncertain timing, and he sees AI and crypto as complementary catalysts.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: Agentic commerce could be a stablecoin demand driver but needs a long horizon.
insights.quote: AI agents will [music] use stablecoins and DeFi protocols and not dollars and centralized protocols

insights.claim: Hougan highlights Venice as a private AI protocol with equity-like exposure and one of the best-performing tokens in recent months, and NEAR as aligned with the theme through its easy intent-signature wallet plus an AI catalyst.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan
insights.so_what: AI-crypto exposure is best taken via leading protocols in a segment rather than a narrow thesis.
